attributes.title: HANFIS prospective evaluation (E7)
attributes.description: Pre-registration of a prospective forward evaluation (E7) of HANFIS, a hierarchical ANFIS for dynamic risk scoring of container deployments, against persistence, a hybrid and a four-parameter formula. Registered before any label for the test weeks (from 2026-08-31) was computed; frozen in git tag e7-prereg-2026-10-12 (commit dbed812, created 2026-10-12 15:04 +0700).
tags: preregistration ANFIS EPSS vulnerability prioritization Kubernetes

344-2.value:
P7a (regime). In the following weeks without a change in EPSS model version, HANFIS is not better than persistence: the upper bound of the 95% CI of its skill score (SS) against persistence is below 0.05.

P7b (hybrid). A fixed blend of HANFIS and persistence, `y_hat = 0.5109 * y_HANFIS + 0.4891 * y_lag4, beats persistence: SS >= 0.05 and the lower 95% bound > 0.
P7d (information beyond persistence; secondary). The mean weekly Spearman correlation between predicted change (`y_HANFIS - y_lag4`) and realized change (`y - y_lag4`) has a lower 95% bound > 0.

P7e (second family; post hoc origin). A four-parameter formula `y_hat = a + b * max(x2, c * x7)` (x2 = the exploitability input, x7 = the KEV indicator, both at time t), fitted once on the same training rows as the HANFIS models and then frozen (`protocols/E7_formula_2026-10-12.json`), beats persistence: SS >= 0.05 and the lower 95% bound > 0.

P7f (second family; post hoc origin). HANFIS is not better than that formula: the upper bound of the 95% CI of the HANFIS skill score against the formula is below 0.05 (refuted if SS >= 0.05 with a lower bound > 0).

- P7c (precision at 20% on levels) is descriptive only: persistence already reaches 0.969 on earlier data, a ceiling effect that makes it uninformative.

344-4.value: Authors have observed the data, but have not performed the proposed analyses. At least some of the data that will be used for this analysis plan has been accessed and observed by the authors. The authors have sufficiently observed relevant evidence to influence their analysis decisions or conclusions. However, the authors have not yet performed any of the proposed analyses in this plan and will not do so until after this plan is registered.

344-14.value:
Foreknowledge. The authors know the system well from earlier, separately reported analyses of data up to 2026-09-21 (out-of-fold analyses E4 to E14)). That knowledge informed the choice of comparators: the four-parameter formula and hypotheses P7e and P7f are of post hoc origin, formulated after those analyses, and their out-of-fold support is not counted as confirmation. None of the proposed analyses has been run on forward data. The forward outcome labels (test weeks 2026-08-31 to 2026-10-05) have not been computed or observed; no EPSS snapshot after 2026-09-21 has been downloaded; one CISA KEV catalog snapshot dated 2026-09-28 was downloaded before this design (disclosed in the protocol) and has not been used to compute labels; the persistence labels of the first four forward weeks come from weeks 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-24 that belong to the earlier dataset.

Actions to limit unintended influence: the five HANFIS seeds, the blend weight, and the formula coefficients were fixed on training data up to 2026-07-27 and frozen with SHA-256 hashes in git tag e7-prereg-2026-10-12 (commit dbed812) before any forward data were accessed; hypotheses, thresholds, exclusion and sufficiency rules are fixed in the protocol; the evaluation scripts verify the tag and run only once; rehearsals used earlier data only. After the freeze and before this registration, further post hoc analyses (E15 to E20), including a power simulation on earlier clean out-of-fold data that estimated roughly a 50 to 70% chance of confirming P7e, were run on earlier data; none used forward data, and none changed the frozen protocol.

value: Non-randomized study: Does not include random assignment of subjects to treatments or conditions. This usually includes correlational studies, observational studies, surveys, natural experiments, real-world evidence studies, regression discontinuity designs, and descriptive studies.
No causal relationship inferred: This study is not intended to inform a causal relationship.

344-38.value: No treatments are assigned, so blinding of treatments does not apply. The authors are not blind to the design or to results on earlier data, but no forward outcome has been computed or observed. Procedures to remove unintended influences: (1) the five model files, the hybrid weight, the formula coefficients, the analysis scripts and the protocol are frozen and hashed in git tag e7-prereg-2026-10-12 (commit dbed812; SHA-256 of 23 files in the attached freeze record) before forward data are accessed; (2) the evaluation scripts verify the tag against the working files and refuse to run otherwise, and run only once; (3) forward snapshots are downloaded and labels computed only after this registration, by one scripted pipeline with a fixed stage order; (4) the vulnerability database used for the rescan is frozen once on the data date; (5) no tuning on forward data is possible, since all parameters are fixed files; (6) any deviation will be reported as such.

344-40.value:
Prospective, forward-in-time, out-of-sample evaluation of frozen predictors of realised exploitability exposure for container images (observational; no intervention, no treatment assignment, no randomization). Unit of observation: image-week (up to 120 images x 6 weeks = 720 asset-weeks, fewer if images drop out under the pre-registered data-sufficiency rule). Test weeks: the six Mondays 2026-08-31, 09-07, 09-14, 09-21, 09-28 and 10-05, so that each label (realised exposure over the following four weeks, computed from weekly EPSS and CISA KEV snapshots) has matured by the data date D2 = 2026-11-02 (fallback 2026-11-09 only if fewer than six weeks have matured).

Predictors, all frozen before any forward data are accessed: (1) HANFIS, a hierarchical adaptive neuro-fuzzy model (mean of five seeds, trained on labelled weeks up to 2026-07-27, with an embargo of at least 30 days before the first test week); (2) persistence (the label of week t-4); (3) a fixed hybrid of HANFIS and persistence (weight 0.5109); (4) a four-parameter formula y = a + bmax(x2, cx7) (a = 0.1193, b = 98.85, c = 0.10) fitted once on the same training rows.

Comparisons are paired within image-week: skill scores (1 - MSE of the model / MSE of the reference) with a bootstrap clustered by image. There are two families of confirmatory hypotheses, each with its own Holm correction: {P7a, P7b} (HANFIS and the hybrid against persistence) and {P7e, P7f} (the formula against persistence, and HANFIS against the formula; hypotheses of post hoc origin). P7c and P7d are descriptive or secondary. Data acquisition and analysis run through one fixed scripted pipeline (scripts/e7_d2.py: fetch, rescan, build, predict, evaluate, formula) only after this registration. The full description is in the attached protocol E7_preregistration_2026-10-12.md.

344-47.value:
Population and frame: the 120 container images of the pre-defined inventory (digest-pinned; the same inventory as in the earlier dataset), observed weekly. Sources: public weekly EPSS score archives and CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog snapshots, downloaded only after this registration and sealed with a manifest of SHA-256 hashes; image vulnerability data from Trivy scans of the digest-pinned images, rescanned once on the data date D2 with a vulnerability database frozen on that day.

Sample: all image-weeks t with t + 28 days <= D2. Primary D2 = 2026-11-02 (six weeks: 2026-08-31 to 2026-10-05); fallback D2 = 2026-11-09 only if fewer than six weeks are usable when the dataset is built, decided before any model is run on forward data. With fewer than six usable weeks the study is postponed, not relaxed.

Exclusion criteria (fixed in the protocol): rows with unresolved vulnerability-range evidence (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE) are dropped only if they are at most 2% of test-week rows, and an image that loses all of its test weeks leaves the analysis and is reported (cockroachdb is expected to). If the EPSS model version changes inside the evaluation window, the affected weeks are handled as a separate break regime as specified in the protocol.

Duration: data collection and analysis run in one scripted session on D2 (scripts/e7_d2.py: fetch, rescan, build, predict, evaluate, formula). The full description is in the attached protocol E7_preregistration_2026-10-12.md.

344-51.value: Up to 120 images x 6 forward weeks = 720 asset-weeks (unit of analysis: image-week), about 714 if cockroachdb drops out as expected. There are about 119 image clusters because the two variants of the control image share one scan, and fewer if images drop out. The sample is the same for all predictors, since every predictor is evaluated on the same asset-weeks (paired design). Bootstrap resampling is clustered by image (2,000 resamples per image).

344-53.value: The sample size is fixed by the inventory (120 images) and by the number of weeks whose four-week labels have matured by the data date; it is not chosen by a power calculation. A post hoc simulation on earlier clean out-of-fold data (not forward data), run after the git freeze and before this registration, estimated the probability of confirming P7e at about 50% (all clean windows) to 70% (new-model windows), and of supporting P7f at about 100%. A non-confirmation of P7e will therefore be reported as “not demonstrated”, not as evidence against the formula.

344-55.value:
Starting: forward data are fetched and labels computed only after this registration and after verification of the git tag e7-prereg-2026-10-12. The pipeline starts on the data date D2 = 2026-11-02 (a Monday). Stopping: data collection ends when the weekly snapshots up to D2 have been downloaded and the six test weeks have matured; there is no sequential testing, no interim analysis, and no optional stopping. 

Fallback: if fewer than six weeks have matured by the time the dataset is built, the study is postponed to D2 = 2026-11-09, a decision made before any model is run on forward data. Results are never re-run with different criteria (the evaluation scripts run once).

344-58.value: None. This is an observational forward evaluation: no variable is manipulated; there are no treatment arms and no randomization. The compared predictors (HANFIS, persistence, the hybrid, and the four-parameter formula) are fixed model outputs evaluated on the same asset-weeks, not experimental conditions.

344-62.value:
Outcome: the realised exploitability exposure label y(a,t) of image a in week t on a 0-100 scale, computed from weekly EPSS and CISA KEV snapshots over the four weeks after t, as defined in the protocol (definition frozen in the E4 protocol, amendment A-13): the mean over weekly snapshots tau in {t+7, ..., t+28 days} of the maximum over active CVEs v of X_v(tau) x rho_v, with X_v = max(EPSS, KEV indicator) and rho_v the runtime-reachability factor.

Predictor inputs (seven, normalized): x1 CVSS (maximum over affected and reachable CVEs), x2 exploitability (EPSS x reachability), x3 patch risk (0, 1 or 2), x4 MFA risk, x5 Kubernetes exposure, x6 asset criticality (1 to 5), x7 threat intelligence (KEV indicator at t). x4 to x6 are per-asset constants.

Reference and predictors evaluated: persistence (the label of week t-4), HANFIS (mean of five frozen seeds), the hybrid (weight 0.5109), the four-parameter formula y = a + bmax(x2, cx7), and a ridge model on the seven inputs (descriptive only).

Variables used for subsetting or exclusion: version-range status of each CVE (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE rows), EPSS model version of each snapshot, completeness of the snapshot sequence, image identifier and image cluster (for the clustered bootstrap), and, for descriptive strata, whether x2 or the KEV status changed during the previous four weeks.

344-66.value:
Derived variables and indices (exact definitions are in the attached protocol and in the frozen files):

Persistence reference: y_lag4(a,t) = y(a, t - 4 weeks), the realised label of the same image four weeks earlier.
HANFIS prediction: yhat_HANFIS(a,t) = mean of the predictions of the five frozen seeds (20260928, 20261005, 20261012, 20261019, 20261026), trained on labelled weeks up to 2026-07-27.
Hybrid: yhat_hybrid(a,t) = lambda x yhat_HANFIS(a,t) + (1 - lambda) x y_lag4(a,t), with lambda = 0.5109 (fixed file protocols/E7_lambda_2026-10-08.json).
Formula: yhat_formula(a,t) = a0 + b x max(x2, c x x7), with a0 = 0.1193, b = 98.8507 and c = 0.10 (fixed file protocols/E7_formula_2026-10-12.json); x2 = exploitability (EPSS x reachability) and x7 = KEV indicator at t; a missing value is coded 0.
Pooled mean squared error: MSE_m = (1/N) x sum over all N test asset-weeks of (yhat_m(a,t) - y(a,t))^2, on the 0-100 scale.
Skill score: SS(m, r) = 1 - MSE_m / MSE_r for a model m and a reference r (persistence for P7a, P7b and P7e; the formula for P7f).
Descriptive and secondary indices: precision at the top 20% of predicted risk (P7c); the Spearman correlation between predicted change (yhat - y_lag4) and realised change (y - y_lag4) (P7d), both as defined in the protocol; and an input-change indicator equal to 1 if x2 or the KEV status at t differs from its value four weeks earlier, used only for descriptive strata.

344-71.value:
Predictive accuracy is compared using the pooled mean squared error (MSE) over all test asset-weeks, on the raw 0-100 scale. For a model m and a reference r, the skill score is SS = 1 - MSE_m / MSE_r. All comparisons are paired on the same asset-weeks. Uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals from a cluster bootstrap that resamples images (2,000 resamples, seed 20261102); the two variants of the control image form one cluster.

Confirmatory one-sided tests (decision rules exactly as stated in the hypotheses and in the attached protocol):

P7a: HANFIS (mean of five frozen seeds) against persistence (the label of week t-4); H0: SS >= 0.05; supported if the upper 95% bound of SS is below 0.05 and the Holm test passes.
P7b: the hybrid (lambda = 0.5109) against persistence; H0: SS <= 0; confirmed if SS >= 0.05, the lower 95% bound is above 0, and the Holm test passes.
P7e: the four-parameter formula (a = 0.1193, b = 98.85, c = 0.10) against persistence; H0: SS <= 0; confirmed if SS >= 0.05, the lower bound is above 0 and the Holm test passes; worse if the upper bound is below 0.
P7f: HANFIS against the formula; H0: SS >= 0.05; supported if the upper bound is below 0.05 and the Holm test passes; refuted if SS >= 0.05 with the lower bound above 0.

One-sided p-values come from the bootstrap distribution with a +1 correction. No other models, covariates, or interactions are fitted; all predictors are frozen before accessing the forward data.

344-75.value: None for the confirmatory analyses: the outcome and the predictions are used on the raw 0-100 scale. The input normalizations are fixed scalings inside the frozen model files and are not re-estimated. A log1p-scaled outcome is reported only as a secondary descriptive check. There are no categorical predictors in the confirmatory models.

344-77.value: One-sided tests at alpha = 0.025 per family, with a Holm correction within each of two separate families: family 1 {P7a, P7b} and family 2 {P7e, P7f}; thresholds of 0.0125 for the smaller p-value and 0.025 for the larger; the combined one-sided error is at most 0.05. p-values are one-sided bootstrap p-values, (1 + number of resamples beyond the null) / (B + 1) with B = 2,000. Smallest effect size of interest: SS = 0.05. A hypothesis is supported or confirmed only if both its interval criterion and its Holm test are met; otherwise the result is reported as “not demonstrated”, never as equivalence. A week-clustered bootstrap is reported as a sensitivity analysis without criteria; a result that meets its criterion under image-clustered inference but not under the week-clustered sensitivity will be reported as “confirmed by image-clustered inference, fragile by week-clustered inference”.

344-79.value: All image weeks from the six test weeks of the predefined inventory are included. Exclusions, fixed in the protocol: (1) weeks without a complete snapshot sequence (reported); (2) rows with unresolved vulnerability-range evidence (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE) are dropped only if they amount to at most 2% of test-week rows (at most 14 of 720); an image that loses all of its test weeks leaves the forward analysis and is reported (cockroachdb is expected to, having unresolved evidence for seven consecutive weeks from 2026-08-10); beyond 2% the analysis is put on hold; (3) weeks after a change of the EPSS model version inside the evaluation window are analysed separately as a break regime; (4) rows without the lag-4 label are excluded from the comparisons that need it. No outliers are removed.

344-81.value: Unknown inputs are handled as in the training data (a missing value is coded as 0 for the model) and are excluded only from the descriptive input-change strata. Rows without the lag-4 persistence label are excluded from the comparisons that need it. No imputation is performed; weeks without a complete snapshot sequence are excluded and reported.

344-83.value:
Descriptive or secondary, reported without confirmatory criteria: P7c (precision at the top 20% of predicted risk, hybrid against persistence; non-inferiority is reported descriptively because persistence is near its ceiling, 0.969 on earlier data); P7d (weekly Spearman correlation between predicted change and realised change relative to the lag-4 label; informative if the lower 95% bound is above 0); skill by strata of input change available at time t (change of exploitability or KEV status over four weeks); per-fold blend weights; a log1p scale; results without the image “wordpress”; a ridge model on the seven inputs; and the week-clustered bootstrap sensitivity.

Power is limited. On earlier out-of-fold data the hybrid’s SS was 0.174 (95% CI 0.011 to 0.236, Holm p 0.021, above the 0.0125 threshold). Results that are not significant are reported as not demonstrated, not as equivalence. On historical six-week windows (post hoc, overlapping), the formula’s advantage over persistence met its criterion in about one third of windows, and a post hoc simulation on earlier clean out-of-fold data, run after the git freeze, estimated about 50 to 70% for confirming P7e and about 100% for supporting P7f; a non-confirmation of P7e must therefore not be read as a refutation. The image-clustered bootstrap treats weekly shocks shared by all images as fixed, and with six weeks the effective number of time points is six; in out-of-fold data (45 weeks) the week-clustered 95% CI for the formula’s skill against persistence (0.127 to 0.672) was about three times wider than the image-clustered one (0.263 to 0.425).

344-86.value:
Hypotheses P7a, P7b, and P7d derive from a post hoc analysis of E4 data and from a rehearsal of the analysis code on out-of-fold predictions (not on forward data). The formula and hypotheses P7e and P7f originate from post hoc analyses of the same out-of-fold data (their out-of-fold support is not counted as confirmation); the formula coefficients are fixed before any forward label is computed. The target does not depend on the three environmental inputs, so this study cannot test their value. An earlier explanation-fidelity study (E6) was run under a protocol whose version-control freeze did not capture the final protocol text; that deviation is documented and does not affect E7.

Registration history. A first registration of this protocol was initiated from project 9ezg4 on 2026-10-12 at about 16:59 +0700 (09:59 UTC; draft 6acca8dcad5cbbc6a330cf43). It did not complete: OSF showed no completed registration and sent no confirmation. On the advice of OSF Support, this registration (draft 6acdc71921dbef780a8be845) was created with the same protocol. No forward data were fetched or analyzed in between, and the frozen protocol, scripts, and hashes are unchanged.


Protocol, scripts, models' hashes, and the blend-weight file at commit dbed812, tag e7-prereg-2026-10-12, created 2026-10-12 15:04:42 +0700.
The attached E7_freeze_record_2026-10-12.txt lists the SHA-256 hashes of the 23 frozen files as stored in the git tag. The repository is github.com/udahafeez7/HANFIS-RESEARCH (currently private; an archived copy with a DOI is planned).

Outcome: the realised exploitability exposure label y(a,t) of image a in week t on a 0-100 scale, computed from weekly EPSS and CISA KEV snapshots over the four weeks after t, as defined in the protocol (definition frozen in the E4 protocol, amendment A-13): the mean over weekly snapshots tau in {t+7, ..., t+28 days} of the maximum over active CVEs v of X_v(tau) x rho_v, with X_v = max(EPSS, KEV indicator) and rho_v the runtime-reachability factor.

Predictor inputs (seven, normalized): x1 CVSS (maximum over affected and reachable CVEs), x2 exploitability (EPSS x reachability), x3 patch risk (0, 1 or 2), x4 MFA risk, x5 Kubernetes exposure, x6 asset criticality (1 to 5), x7 threat intelligence (KEV indicator at t). x4 to x6 are per-asset constants.

Reference and predictors evaluated: persistence (the label of week t-4), HANFIS (mean of five frozen seeds), the hybrid (weight 0.5109), the four-parameter formula y = a + bmax(x2, cx7), and a ridge model on the seven inputs (descriptive only).

Variables used for subsetting or exclusion: version-range status of each CVE (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE rows), EPSS model version of each snapshot, completeness of the snapshot sequence, image identifier and image cluster (for the clustered bootstrap), and, for descriptive strata, whether x2 or the KEV status changed during the previous four weeks.
registration_responses.344-66:
Derived variables and indices (exact definitions are in the attached protocol and in the frozen files):

Persistence reference: y_lag4(a,t) = y(a, t - 4 weeks), the realised label of the same image four weeks earlier.
HANFIS prediction: yhat_HANFIS(a,t) = mean of the predictions of the five frozen seeds (20260928, 20261005, 20261012, 20261019, 20261026), trained on labelled weeks up to 2026-07-27.
Hybrid: yhat_hybrid(a,t) = lambda x yhat_HANFIS(a,t) + (1 - lambda) x y_lag4(a,t), with lambda = 0.5109 (fixed file protocols/E7_lambda_2026-10-08.json).
Formula: yhat_formula(a,t) = a0 + b x max(x2, c x x7), with a0 = 0.1193, b = 98.8507 and c = 0.10 (fixed file protocols/E7_formula_2026-10-12.json); x2 = exploitability (EPSS x reachability) and x7 = KEV indicator at t; a missing value is coded 0.
Pooled mean squared error: MSE_m = (1/N) x sum over all N test asset-weeks of (yhat_m(a,t) - y(a,t))^2, on the 0-100 scale.
Skill score: SS(m, r) = 1 - MSE_m / MSE_r for a model m and a reference r (persistence for P7a, P7b and P7e; the formula for P7f).
Descriptive and secondary indices: precision at the top 20% of predicted risk (P7c); the Spearman correlation between predicted change (yhat - y_lag4) and realised change (y - y_lag4) (P7d), both as defined in the protocol; and an input-change indicator equal to 1 if x2 or the KEV status at t differs from its value four weeks earlier, used only for descriptive strata.
registration_responses.344-71:
Predictive accuracy is compared using the pooled mean squared error (MSE) over all test asset-weeks, on the raw 0-100 scale. For a model m and a reference r, the skill score is SS = 1 - MSE_m / MSE_r. All comparisons are paired on the same asset-weeks. Uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals from a cluster bootstrap that resamples images (2,000 resamples, seed 20261102); the two variants of the control image form one cluster.

Confirmatory one-sided tests (decision rules exactly as stated in the hypotheses and in the attached protocol):

P7a: HANFIS (mean of five frozen seeds) against persistence (the label of week t-4); H0: SS >= 0.05; supported if the upper 95% bound of SS is below 0.05 and the Holm test passes.
P7b: the hybrid (lambda = 0.5109) against persistence; H0: SS <= 0; confirmed if SS >= 0.05, the lower 95% bound is above 0, and the Holm test passes.
P7e: the four-parameter formula (a = 0.1193, b = 98.85, c = 0.10) against persistence; H0: SS <= 0; confirmed if SS >= 0.05, the lower bound is above 0 and the Holm test passes; worse if the upper bound is below 0.
P7f: HANFIS against the formula; H0: SS >= 0.05; supported if the upper bound is below 0.05 and the Holm test passes; refuted if SS >= 0.05 with the lower bound above 0.

One-sided p-values come from the bootstrap distribution with a +1 correction. No other models, covariates, or interactions are fitted; all predictors are frozen before accessing the forward data.
registration_responses.344-75: None for the confirmatory analyses: the outcome and the predictions are used on the raw 0-100 scale. The input normalizations are fixed scalings inside the frozen model files and are not re-estimated. A log1p-scaled outcome is reported only as a secondary descriptive check. There are no categorical predictors in the confirmatory models.
registration_responses.344-77: One-sided tests at alpha = 0.025 per family, with a Holm correction within each of two separate families: family 1 {P7a, P7b} and family 2 {P7e, P7f}; thresholds of 0.0125 for the smaller p-value and 0.025 for the larger; the combined one-sided error is at most 0.05. p-values are one-sided bootstrap p-values, (1 + number of resamples beyond the null) / (B + 1) with B = 2,000. Smallest effect size of interest: SS = 0.05. A hypothesis is supported or confirmed only if both its interval criterion and its Holm test are met; otherwise the result is reported as “not demonstrated”, never as equivalence. A week-clustered bootstrap is reported as a sensitivity analysis without criteria; a result that meets its criterion under image-clustered inference but not under the week-clustered sensitivity will be reported as “confirmed by image-clustered inference, fragile by week-clustered inference”.
registration_responses.344-79: All image weeks from the six test weeks of the predefined inventory are included. Exclusions, fixed in the protocol: (1) weeks without a complete snapshot sequence (reported); (2) rows with unresolved vulnerability-range evidence (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE) are dropped only if they amount to at most 2% of test-week rows (at most 14 of 720); an image that loses all of its test weeks leaves the forward analysis and is reported (cockroachdb is expected to, having unresolved evidence for seven consecutive weeks from 2026-08-10); beyond 2% the analysis is put on hold; (3) weeks after a change of the EPSS model version inside the evaluation window are analysed separately as a break regime; (4) rows without the lag-4 label are excluded from the comparisons that need it. No outliers are removed.
registration_responses.344-81: Unknown inputs are handled as in the training data (a missing value is coded as 0 for the model) and are excluded only from the descriptive input-change strata. Rows without the lag-4 persistence label are excluded from the comparisons that need it. No imputation is performed; weeks without a complete snapshot sequence are excluded and reported.
registration_responses.344-83:
Descriptive or secondary, reported without confirmatory criteria: P7c (precision at the top 20% of predicted risk, hybrid against persistence; non-inferiority is reported descriptively because persistence is near its ceiling, 0.969 on earlier data); P7d (weekly Spearman correlation between predicted change and realised change relative to the lag-4 label; informative if the lower 95% bound is above 0); skill by strata of input change available at time t (change of exploitability or KEV status over four weeks); per-fold blend weights; a log1p scale; results without the image “wordpress”; a ridge model on the seven inputs; and the week-clustered bootstrap sensitivity.

Power is limited. On earlier out-of-fold data the hybrid’s SS was 0.174 (95% CI 0.011 to 0.236, Holm p 0.021, above the 0.0125 threshold). Results that are not significant are reported as not demonstrated, not as equivalence. On historical six-week windows (post hoc, overlapping), the formula’s advantage over persistence met its criterion in about one third of windows, and a post hoc simulation on earlier clean out-of-fold data, run after the git freeze, estimated about 50 to 70% for confirming P7e and about 100% for supporting P7f; a non-confirmation of P7e must therefore not be read as a refutation. The image-clustered bootstrap treats weekly shocks shared by all images as fixed, and with six weeks the effective number of time points is six; in out-of-fold data (45 weeks) the week-clustered 95% CI for the formula’s skill against persistence (0.127 to 0.672) was about three times wider than the image-clustered one (0.263 to 0.425).
registration_responses.344-86:
Hypotheses P7a, P7b, and P7d derive from a post hoc analysis of E4 data and from a rehearsal of the analysis code on out-of-fold predictions (not on forward data). The formula and hypotheses P7e and P7f originate from post hoc analyses of the same out-of-fold data (their out-of-fold support is not counted as confirmation); the formula coefficients are fixed before any forward label is computed. The target does not depend on the three environmental inputs, so this study cannot test their value.
